answer: Each identity seasons one juniper lot on coastal racks and posts an 80 bond and a rack fee; registry allows one lot per key. An auditor taps each board and reads its echo pitch against the seasoning curve and ocean humidity log: a board too green, too dry, or already registered burns the bond. The k-th rack fee is 35+11(k-1), so the 1000th lot costs 11024 and 1000 fakes pay 5529500 in fees plus 80000 in bonds, total fees growing quadratically. A rented-board ring fails: its echo already belongs to another key. An honest sawyer pays 35 and reclaims 80 after clean seasoning.
